question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose busy, active-run count, and last-run activity through the generic Plugin SDK status contract, with Discord and Telegram sending a visible busy acknowledgement even when ordinary source replies are suppressed?
rationale: The branch is mechanically coherent, but this creates a durable public plugin surface and intentionally changes message-delivery behavior for a user preference; tests and live proof cannot choose that product contract.

options.title: Approve the generic contract
options.body: Accept the additive shared status fields and the Discord/Telegram busy acknowledgements as the supported responsiveness model for channel plugins.

options.title: Keep the status data channel-local
options.body: Request a narrower implementation that reports busy state without expanding the generic Plugin SDK contract, and separately decide whether acknowledgements should respect source-reply suppression.

recommendation.title: Approve the generic contract
recommendation.body: Accept the additive shared status fields and the Discord/Telegram busy acknowledgements as the supported responsiveness model for channel plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is cross-plugin product and API direction, and the current review timeline explicitly routed the PR to this person.
